assessment.reason: The study directly evaluates experimental-design methods for valuing EQ-5D-5L health states. It compares unstratified and severity-stratified designs across three DCE formats. EuroQol Research Foundation support is explicit.

studies.label: Severity-stratified DCE design experiment for EQ-5D-5L health-state valuation
studies.family_rationale: The principal contribution is an evaluation of how severity coverage in experimental designs affects DCE health-state values, prediction bias, and the validity of three valuation formats. The study does not present a value set as its main output.

items.statement: The authors interpret severity stratification as a validity requirement for DCE-duration designs because it reduces extrapolation from a misspecified model and prevents downward bias in poor-state values.
source: Full article, Discussion, first and second paragraphs

items.statement: The authors conclude that differences in severity-range coverage can explain part of the variation between DCE-derived health-state values and advise caution when using such values until the prevalence of extrapolation problems is known.
The study did not examine how specific the results were to the matched pairwise choice format; the fixed full-health alternative and the 10-year impaired-state duration might have amplified the skew.
The study did not compare the merits of efficient designs with other design-generation approaches that might not require severity-spread controls.

The absence of evidence for health-state selection effects in DCE-death might not apply to states from other descriptive systems, including disease-specific systems with different severity distributions.
The normal distribution assumed for parameters might be unsuitable for monotonic attribute-level effects because it is unbounded.
Respondents might not treat equivalent durations expressed in months and years in the same way.

items.label: severity stratification
items.description: A design restriction that divides EQ-5D-5L states into 21 predicted-utility strata and requires each sub-design to include one task from every stratum.
source: Full article, Methods, Experimental Designs With/Without Severity-Stratified Restriction

items.label: extrapolation from a misspecified DCE-duration model
items.description: Bias can occur when an efficient design favors relatively mild states and the multiplicative duration model extrapolates values for poorly represented severe states.
